messages:
marta (CS): heads-up — we just finished the post-incident call for the Dedicated 5xx spike. want to align on the customer-facing follow-up and status page copy before i send. @sam you ok with the proposed credit language?

incident-bot: INCIDENT #2024-172: Increased 5xx rate affecting a subset of Redwood Dedicated customers in us-west-2. Page sent to on-call at 2024-04-02T21:05:12Z.

liam (oncall): quick timeline from ops: ~21:02 alarm triggered for elevated 5xx on router pool. saw sustained errors for ~6m, autoscaler loop thrashing when replicas hit 0 -> then overshot. short term mitigation was a manual scale + pinned fallback model variant, rolled traffic at 21:10. errors began dropping by 21:14. full steady state restored by 21:20 after rolling restart.

raj (SRE): root cause = edge-case in our autoscaler when combined with aggressive eviction during rapid scale-down. reproduced locally with unit test I pushed. fix in flight: patch autoscaler to enforce min-replicas floor during bursty workloads + add a backoff window. will open PR in 10m.

marta (CS): thanks. customers impacted: list attached in support ticket 9872. most saw brief errors (2–6 minutes). two customers had errors on production traffic for ~10 minutes due to longer client retry windows; both were alerted by their apps.

sam (acct exec): suggestion on credits: propose one day of Dedicated service credits pro-rated to incident impact window for customers with >2% error rate during window. low-friction offer for affected accounts. thoughts?

olivia (eng-mgr): agree with conservative credits. also recommend we include what we fixed and next steps (patch rollout ETA + playbook). Ops will schedule the autoscaler patch for a canary in staging tonight and prod rollout tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

marta (CS): okay drafting email. pasting draft below — open to edits before i send to affected accounts:

----BEGIN CUSTOMER DRAFT----
Hi <Customer Name>,

We’re reaching out about a service interruption that affected your Redwood Dedicated capacity on 2024-04-02 between 21:02–21:20 UTC. During this window some requests returned 5xx errors. Our engineers rolled a mitigation and restored steady state by 21:20.

What happened: an autoscaler bug caused replica churn under bursty scale-down, which briefly led to failed inferences for a subset of requests.

What we did: manually pinned a stable model variant and performed a rolling restart to restore capacity. We have a patch to the autoscaler to prevent this behavior and will canary it in staging tonight, with a targeted production rollout on 2024-04-03 02:00 UTC.

What we’re doing next: patching the autoscaler, adding a guardrail in the orchestration layer to maintain min-replicas during scale down bursts, and adding monitoring alerts to detect similar patterns earlier.

Credit: we’re offering a pro-rated Dedicated service credit for the impacted window.

If you’d like a private post-incident call, we can schedule one.

Regards,
The Redwood Inference Team
----END CUSTOMER DRAFT----

alice (docs): small wording suggestion — change "service interruption" to "service incident" and clarify that "some requests" means a small percentage of traffic. reduces alarm.

marta (CS): good call — updated. also adding a one-paragraph timeline for the status page. proposed status page update below — please sign off:

----BEGIN STATUS PAGE----
Incident: Increased 5xx errors for Redwood Dedicated customers in us-west-2
Status: Resolved
Impact: Some customers experienced transient 5xx errors between 2024-04-02 21:02 UTC and 2024-04-02 21:20 UTC.
Summary: An autoscaling bug caused rapid replica churn under a bursty scale-down condition, briefly reducing capacity for a subset of requests. Mitigation included manual scaling, pinning a stable model variant, and a rolling restart.
Next steps: A patch to the autoscaler will be canaried in staging tonight and rolled to production on 2024-04-03 02:00 UTC. We will follow up once the rollout completes.
----END STATUS PAGE----

raj (SRE): status page looks fine. one tweak: change "reducing capacity" -> "temporarily reducing available instances" for clarity.

marta (CS): done. sam — will you approve the credit wording?

sam (acct exec): approved. keep it simple: "pro-rated service credit for the incident window." No need to overcommit on amount until impact is calculated. :thumbsup:

liam (oncall): ops action items from call: 1) PR + tests for autoscaler fix (raj) 2) add integration test simulating bursty scale-down (raj) 3) canary deploy in staging tonight (ops) 4) prod rollout 02:00 UTC (ops) 5) update runbook and add quick-check alert (alice + raj) 6) send CS-approved customer email and status page update (marta).

marta (CS): tagging timeline clarifications — customers often ask exact request counts. we have aggregated metrics in ticket 9872 but will include percent impacted and approximate request counts where possible. do not include raw logs in email.

olivia (eng-mgr): also plan a retrospective with SRE + infra to discuss autoscaler long-term behavior. will schedule next week.

marta (CS): final checklist before send:
- [x] status page copy agreed
- [x] customer email draft agreed
- [x] credit language approved by sales
- [ ] confirm final impacted account list + exact windows from support ticket
- [ ] schedule customer calls for any accounts requesting them

(5m later)

marta (CS): sending email to affected customers now, will post status page update in 5. ping me if you want to review before publish.

sam (acct exec): thanks team — i’ll follow up with our two customers who had longer exposure and book calls as needed.

incident-bot: STATUS PAGE UPDATED: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2024-172 at 2024-04-02T21:35:12Z

marta (CS): closing thread — will open a follow-up thread once patch is fully rolled and we have post-rollout verification. :white_check_mark:
